<reason>CON wins the decisive clashes: the soda/farming loophole shows a bottling-only ban does little to protect the aquifer hydrologically, and the enforceability dilemma undercuts PRO's claim that permits must fail while other industries can be regulated. CON also answers drought-trigger pressure with automatic telemetry, shut-down-first permits, and corporate bonds. PRO's public-control and direct-competition frame remains plausible, but its relocation and core-asset claims sit uneasily together and never fully neutralize the arbitrariness charge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 and closing dilemma: if governments can enforce automatic cutoffs, regulated permits suffice; if they cannot, exempting vastly larger soda, farm, and industrial extractors leaves the aquifer unprotected anyway.</best_rebuttal>
